title: Etale scheme patching across a closed-integral Ferrand pushout
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:Z\to T$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $j$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and for every $t\in T$ there is an affine open $A\subseteq X$ containing $i(j^{-1}(\{t\}))$. Let $P=X\amalg_ZT$ be a scheme pushout [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with its induced map to $S$. All fibre products below are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $u:X'\to X$ and $v:T'\to T$ are separated etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], where separated means that the relative diagonal is a closed immersion, and let $\phi:X'\times_XZ\xrightarrow{\sim}T'\times_TZ$ be an isomorphism over $Z$. Set $Z'=X'\times_XZ$, use $\phi$ for its map to $T'$, and use its projection for its map to $X'$. Then the scheme pushout $P'=X'\amalg_{Z'}T'$ exists. Its induced morphism $P'\to P$ is separated and etale, and the canonical morphisms
$$X'\longrightarrow P'\times_PX,\qquad T'\longrightarrow P'\times_PT,\qquad Z'\longrightarrow P'\times_PZ$$
are isomorphisms, respecting the specified $\phi$ and all the projections. Conversely, for every etale scheme morphism $q:U\to P$, the inverse-image square with vertices $U\times_PZ$, $U\times_PX$, $U\times_PT$, and $U$ is a pushout in schemes. In this converse $q$ need not be separated or quasi-compact. There are no Noetherian, finite-type, surjectivity, or nilpotence assumptions beyond the stated hypotheses; empty schemes are allowed.

source.place: Tags 0ECK (lemma-pushout-functor) and 0ECL (lemma-pushout-functor-equivalence-flat), etale case, with the canonical unit and counit; the counit for arbitrary etale U follows by Zariski gluing of the separated etale counit.

proof.text: The isomorphism $\phi$ makes both squares in the diagram $(X',Z',T')\to(X,Z,T)$ cartesian. Thus $i':Z'\to X'$ is a closed immersion and $j':Z'\to T'$ is integral. For $t'\in T'$ over $t\in T$, its fibre $F=Z'_{t'}$ is affine, with coordinate ring integral over $\kappa(t')$: apply integral base change and the affine definition of integrality. In particular $|F|$ is quasi-compact. Its image $K\subset X'$ is contained in $u^{-1}A$ for an affine open $A\subset X$ containing $i(j^{-1}(\{t\}))$.

source.place: Tag 0ECK, first paragraph: checking Situation 0ECI for the primed diagram

proof.text: Cover $K$ by finitely many affine opens of $u^{-1}A$ and let $Q$ be their union. Then $Q$ is a quasi-compact open containing $K$. The map $Q\to A$ is separated: its diagonal is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of $u$ on the open $Q\times_AQ$. It is quasi-compact since $Q$ is quasi-compact and $A$ is affine, by qcqs permanence. For every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq Q$ mapping into an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq A$, the composite of the open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}S\hookrightarrow X'$ (etale) with $u$ is etale, hence so is $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ (an etale map into the open $\operatorname{Spec}R'$), and by the affine criterion $R'\to S$ is an etale ring map. Such ring maps are finitely generated and quasi-finite at every prime, and such charts cover the inverse image in $Q$ of every affine open of $A$, so $Q\to A$ is locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite. Zariski's Main Theorem in the form [lemma-nagata-zmt-quasi-affine-source] now shows $Q$ is quasi-affine.

source.place: Tag 0ECK, first paragraph, using Tag 0AP9 (separated locally quasi-finite implies ind-quasi-affine) via the existing quasi-compact ZMT node

proof.text: Embed the quasi-affine scheme $Q$ as an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The composite $F\to Q\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ comes from a ring map to the integral $\kappa(t')$-algebra of step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-field-image-principal-neighbourhood] to the open $Q\subset\operatorname{Spec}R$. It gives a principal affine open $D(f)$ with $K\subset D(f)\subset Q$. Hence every fibre of $j'$ has its image in an affine open of $X'$, exactly the extra hypothesis for the Ferrand scheme pushout theorem. If $F$ is empty one may instead use the empty affine open; the same theorem permits the zero algebra.

source.place: Tag 0ECK, first paragraph, last sentence; Tag 0E21 in its affine ambient-space form

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] to $i',j'$ with the affine-neighbourhood condition established above. It constructs $P'=X'\amalg_{Z'}T'$. The maps $X'\to X\to P$ and $T'\to T\to P$ agree on $Z'$, so the pushout universal property defines $r:P'\to P$. The given $P$ is canonically the Ferrand pushout by uniqueness of scheme pushouts. We may therefore use the quotient topology, compatible affine covers and restriction to opens in that theorem for both pushouts.

source.place: Tags 0E25 and 0ECK, existence of the two pushouts

proof.text: Choose a compatible affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset P$, with $X_W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $T_W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $Z_W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $R=A\times_CB$, where $A\twoheadrightarrow C$. Let $X'_W,T'_W,Z'_W$ be the inverse images of $r^{-1}W$ in $X',T',Z'$; since $ra'=au$ and $rb'=bv$ they are $u^{-1}(X_W)$, $v^{-1}(T_W)$ and $X'_W\times_XZ$. These restricted data satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout]: $i'_W$ is a closed immersion and $j'_W$ is integral (open restrictions of $i',j'$, with the same fibres), and for $t'\in T'_W$ over $t\in T_W$ every $z\in j^{-1}(t)$ has $c(z)=b(t)\in W$, so $i(j^{-1}(\{t\}))\subseteq X_W$; steps 1--3 with the affine open $X_W$ in place of $A$ then give an affine open $D(f)\subseteq Q\subseteq X'_W$ containing $i'(j'^{-1}(\{t'\}))$. By the open-restriction clause of [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] for $P'$, $r^{-1}W$ is a pushout of these restricted data, hence canonically their Ferrand pushout. Its compatible affine cover gives charts $V=\operatorname{Spec}E$ with inverse images $\operatorname{Spec}A_1$, $\operatorname{Spec}B_1$, $\operatorname{Spec}C_1$ and $E=A_1\times_{C_1}B_1$. The original cartesian component squares, restricted to these opens, give the specified algebra identification $C_1=A_1/IA_1\cong B_1\otimes_BC$, where $I=\ker(A\to C)$. These are canonical identifications, using $\phi$, not arbitrary choices of an isomorphic algebra.

source.place: Tag 0ECK, second paragraph: the affine ring diagrams; Tag 0E25, compatible affine covering

proof.text: The maps $A\to A_1$ and $B\to B_1$ are etale: they are affine-chart restrictions of $u,v$. Ring patching [lem-sfb-fibre-product-algebra-etale], with $(A',A,B,C',D)=(A,C,B,A_1,B_1)$ in its notation, shows $R\to E$ is etale. Thus $V\to W$ is etale by the affine criterion. These $V$ cover $P'$ and these $W$ cover $P$, so locality of etaleness gives that $r$ is etale.

Apply [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change] to the underlying modules of the same algebra diagram. It identifies $E\otimes_RA\to A_1$ and $E\otimes_RB\to B_1$ with the canonical projection-induced maps and proves both are bijective. They are ring maps, so they are ring isomorphisms. The affine fibre-product formula therefore makes $X'\to P'\times_PX$ and $T'\to P'\times_PT$ isomorphisms over each $V$, hence globally. Their inverses agree on overlaps because they invert the same canonical maps. Applying the fibre-product universal property once more to $Z'=X'\times_XZ$ gives the third isomorphism. The projection formulas for the module maps and the common algebra $C_1$ show that all these isomorphisms respect $\phi$ and every projection.

source.place: Tag 0ECK, second paragraph, cartesian squares from Tag 07RU

proof.text: For separatedness fix a chart $W\subset P$ as in step 5. Step 7 identifies the inverse images of $X_W,T_W$ in the restricted primed square with the base changes $X'_W\to X_W$ and $T'_W\to T_W$ of $u,v$. They are separated by separated base change. Since $X_W,T_W$ are affine, their sources $X'_W,T'_W$ are separated schemes by [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated]. The separatedness clause of [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] applied over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ says that their pushout $r^{-1}W$ is a separated scheme. Its relative diagonal over $W$ is the pullback of its absolute diagonal along $(r^{-1}W)\times_W(r^{-1}W)\to(r^{-1}W)\times_{\mathbf Z}(r^{-1}W)$, hence is closed. Thus $r^{-1}W\to W$ is separated. Target-open locality proves $r$ separated without assuming either original component is separated over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0ECK, separatedness assertion; use Tag 0E26 locally instead of its universally-closed-surjection proof

proof.text:
Now let $q:U\to P$ be any etale morphism. Choose an affine chart $H_0=\operatorname{Spec}H\subset U$ mapping into a compatible chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $P$. The map $R\to H$ is flat, since etale morphisms are flat. Write $R=A\times_CB$ as in step 5. The flat-algebra clause of [lem-sfb-fibre-product-algebra-flat-presentation] gives the canonical ring isomorphism
$$H\xrightarrow{\sim}(H\otimes_RA)\times_{H\otimes_RC}(H\otimes_RB).$$
The affine fibre-product formula identifies these three tensor algebras with the inverse images of $X,T,Z$ over $H_0$. The map $H\otimes_RA\to H\otimes_RC$ is surjective: $C=A/I$, so its target is $(H\otimes_RA)/I(H\otimes_RA)$. The affine closed-pinching pushout theorem now makes this inverse-image square a pushout with vertex $H_0$. This works for every such affine chart, including charts in any intersection of two opens of $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ECL, converse and final flat-algebra assertion of Tag 08KQ; affine pushout Tag 0ET0

proof.text: To verify the global universal property, fix an arbitrary scheme $Y$ and compatible maps $U\times_PX\to Y$, $U\times_PT\to Y$. Step 9 produces a unique map $H_0\to Y$ on each affine chart $H_0$ mapping into a compatible chart of $P$. These charts cover $U$ by the affine-open basis. On the intersection of two charts, refine by affine opens mapping into a compatible chart of $P$; on each refinement the two candidate maps agree by the uniqueness in step 9. Scheme-morphism gluing therefore gives a unique map $U\to Y$ with the required restrictions. Uniqueness is checked on the same cover. This proves the asserted pushout for arbitrary $q$, without separatedness or quasi-compactness. In fact this last argument uses only flatness of $q$.

source.place: Tag 0ECL, affine counit extended by Zariski gluing; the gluing argument is written out here

proof_origin.place: Tags 0ECK and 0ECL; affine inputs 0E25, 0E21, 07RU, 08KQ and 0ET0. The arbitrary-etale counit is the explicit Zariski gluing of the flat affine counit.
